The strategy will exploit the phenomenon where stocks exhibit mean-reverting behavior within volatile regimes. During periods of high volatility, stock prices tend to fluctuate more widely around their trendline. This can create opportunities for trend following, as price movements are likely to revert towards a recent trend after an extreme deviation.

This persistence might arise due to market psychology and information processing, where traders overreact to news, leading to overshooting in price movements. Over time, these exaggerated moves often lead to corrections that follow the initial trend direction.

The rule for this strategy would scale position sizes based on volatility: when volatility is high, reduce position size; during low-volatility periods, increase position size. This ensures that you are more cautious during volatile times and can capitalize on trends when market movements become less erratic.

The strategy relies on computing volatility to determine position sizes. For each stock, calculate the 20-day rolling standard deviation of daily returns as the primary signal. This measure captures recent price fluctuations and indicates volatile regimes.

On a given day, rank all candidate stocks based on their calculated 20-day volatility. Stocks with lower volatility are ranked higher, as they present better trend-following opportunities during low-volatility periods. For high volatility days, the opposite ranking is applied, prioritizing stocks with higher volatility to maintain caution and reduce position sizes.

This ranking helps in deciding which stocks to enter or exit based on their relative volatility, ensuring that the strategy adapts dynamically to market conditions.

This strategy will hold a portfolio of up to 30 stocks, with positions sized based on their volatility ranking. During low-volatility periods, weights can range from 2% to 5%, ensuring balanced exposure. In high-volatility regimes, position sizes are reduced to maintain a maximum portfolio loss limit of 5% within any single day, protecting against extreme market movements.
